notes: Cox proportional-hazards model with a matched-pair frailty (b[pair] ~ normal(0,sigma)), rendered from the Stan counting-process (Poisson) likelihood in leukfr.stan. Response obs_t is survival time (weeks); fail is the event/censoring indicator, placed in ignore per the brms kidney census rule; Z is the treatment covariate; pair is the matched-pair grouping factor (21 pairs, 2 obs each). published model = Stan BUGS example.

formula: Y ~ LRT + VR_1 + VR_2 + Gender + School_gender_1 + School_gender_2 + School_denom_1 + School_denom_2 + School_denom_3 + (1 + LRT + VR_1 | school)
notes: Multivariate hierarchical model (schools.stan): per-school random coefficients alpha[school] = random intercept plus random slopes on LRT and VR_1 (alpha ~ multi_normal(gamma,Sigma)); fixed effects on LRT^2, VR_2, Gender, School_gender_1/2 and School_denom_1/2/3; heteroscedastic residual variance exp(-(theta+phi*LRT)). Rendered from Stan. school is the grouping factor (38 schools, 1978 pupils). The LRT^2 quadratic and the variance model are not representable in the registry (LRT filed once per the census polynomial rule). Y is a standardised exam score. published model = Stan BUGS example.

Normal hierarchical linear growth model (hepatitis.stan): per-patient random intercept alpha[idxn1] and random slope beta[idxn1] on time, both exchangeable (alpha ~ normal(alpha0,sigma_alpha), beta ~ normal(beta0,sigma_beta)); rendered from Stan. Response Yvec1 = log HBV titre, tvec1 = time, idxn1 = patient index (106 patients, 2-3 obs each). The group-level baseline covariate y0 (per-patient, length 106) is not in the table, so it is not named as a covariate (brief rule). published model = Stan BUGS example.
